sources.title: Digitalis purpurea — Kew Species Profile
sources.quote: common foxglove is also a source of digitoxin, used in the heart drug digitalis.
sources.note: Use digitoxin rather than repeating the Wikipedia introduction's digoxin wording. Kew also confirms cardiac glycosides throughout the plant.

sources.title: Oenanthe crocata — RHS
sources.quote: Hemlock water dropwort is an extremely poisonous, perennial plant.

sources.title: St. John’s Wort — NCCIH
sources.quote: St. John’s wort can interact in dangerous, sometimes life-threatening ways with a variety of medicines.
sources.note: Corroborates serious medicine interactions; no treatment recommendation is inferred.

sources.title: Oleandrin — Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
sources.quote: Consumption of this botanical may be fatal.
sources.note: Patient Warnings identifies the raw Nerium oleander plant as highly toxic.

sources.title: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids in borage — profiling and quantification study (2023)
sources.quote: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PA) from borage (Borago officinalis) consumed as herb and tea, may pose a food safety risk.
sources.note: Primary analytical study corroborates the presence of PAs; culinary history is not general permission to eat the plant.

sources.title: Milk Thistle — NCCIH
sources.quote: did not show benefits from supplementation with the milk thistle extract silymarin.
sources.note: NCCIH describes conflicting/limited liver-disease trials and two funded studies (hepatitis C and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis) without benefit. This replaces the Wikipedia article's outdated blanket claim about no clinical evidence.

sources.title: Ragwort — RHS Advice
sources.quote: The ingestion of green or dried ragwort by grazing animals can cause serious liver damage and can be fatal.
sources.note: Confirms danger of both green and dried material, alongside value to insects.

sources.title: Crofton weed — Queensland Government
sources.quote: causes Tallebudgera Horse Disease, which results in serious respiratory damage and death.
sources.note: Corroborates horse toxicity. Passage available in the search result; direct page retrieval timed out.
